reason: Both sets cover the same facets (SUMOylation, nucleocytoplasmic transport/nuclear pore, nuclear envelope remodelling, mitotic spindle/AURKA-TPX2, cell cycle), but B repeats the mitotic spindle/centrosome context in about 20 heavily overlapping themes, while A gives each context at a few clean levels.

Beyond the shared NMDA/AMPA signalling and LTP/CREB themes, B adds a broader postsynaptic organisation theme (NMDA/AMPA receptor clustering, receptor transport to the postsynaptic membrane, PSD assembly). That theme speaks directly to receptor assembly and surface delivery, and it is worth a few extra near-duplicate small themes.

A covers the cholinergic synapse, toxin/release-cycle, NMJ assembly and neurotransmitter-transporter contexts in 9 themes; B repeats them as near-duplicates and adds several catecholamine-only themes with no cholinergic or choline-uptake content.

The two sets are nearly identical (UPR/ATF6-XBP1 core, SREBP/cholesterol, FOXO/NRF2 stress, ER translocation, chaperone folding), but B adds redundant copies of the chaperone and ER-translocation themes without any new context.

Both reduce the target to the E-cadherin/adherens-junction context and miss the BRCA1 facet; A gives that context as a clean 6-theme size ladder, while B splits it into about 16 nearly identical junction themes.

Both cover the TGN retrograde/lysosomal sorting, COPI/Golgi, Golgi organisation and broader secretory/endosomal recycling contexts, but B spreads them over about 28 heavily overlapping themes, while A gives a readable 12-theme hierarchy with the same content.
